orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rajiv Sharma
orders.text:
S.A. No. 126 of 2013 
Hon’ble U.C. Dhyani, J. Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the 
appellants. 
 None is present for the respondents 
despite service of notice. Affidavit of service 
has been filed on behalf of the appellants to 
indicate that the respondents are duly served. 
 Respondent no. 4 died on 14.10.2013. 
An intimation to this effect was given to the 
Court on 25.11.2013. The Court permitted the 
appellants to take steps within three weeks, but 
the steps were not taken in time. Thereafter, 
winter vacations followed. Steps were taken 
when the Court reopened after winter break, 
hence, applications are filed by the appellants 
for setting aside abatement, for condoning the 
delay in filing the substitution application and 
for substituting the legal heirs of deceased 
respondent no. 4. 
 All such applications are allowed turn￾by-turn. 
 Abatement of the appeal is set aside. 
Setting aside abatement application no. 1991 of 
2014 is allowed. 
 Being satisfied with the sufficiency of 
reasons furnished by appellant no. 4 in his 
affidavit, delay in filing the substitution 
application is condoned. Delay condonation 
application no. 1902 of 2014 is allowed. 
Consequently, substitution application (CLMA 
no. 1992 of 2014) is also allowed. 
 The appellants are permitted to add the 
word ‘dead’ after the name of respondent no. 4 
and incorporate the names of his legal heirs / 
legal representatives in the memo of appeal. 
 Let amended memo of the parties be 
filed within a week. 
 List on 04.07.2014, for admission. 
 
(U.C. Dhyani, J.) 
 25.06.2014 HN

orders.text:
SA No.126/13 
Hon’ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 Mr. Siddhartha SIngh, Advocate for the appellants. 
 Mr. Alok Mehra, Advocate for the respondents. 
 Respondent no.1-Gopal Ram, in fact, died during 
pendency of first appeal but somehow, the fact of his death 
could not come to the notice of plaintiff/appellants. So, his 
heirs were not impleaded. Gopal Ram is the brother of 
respondent nos.2, 3 and 4. After the death of respondent no.4 
Tika Ram, his heirs were substituted. 
 I think that for effective adjudication, the heirs of Gopal 
Ram should also be substituted. 
 The second appeal is always continuation of original suit 
as well as of the first appeal. 
 Thus, the substitution application (CLMA 13071/14) is 
allowed. Let the substitution be made and the heirs of Gopal 
Ram be impleaded within three days. Thereafter, the service 
shall be effected upon the newly added heirs wherefor the 
steps shall be taken within next one week. 
 Objection filed on behalf of respondent no.1 against the 
substitution application is rejected. 
 At the same time, delay condonation application in 
setting aside abatement (CLMA 13069/14) as well as the 
setting aside application (CLMA 13070/14) are, accordingly, 
set aside. 
 List after service report. 
(Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) 
 17.03.2015 
Rdang

orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rajiv Sharma,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Alok Singh,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Manoj Kumar Tiwari
orders.text:
SA No. 126 of 2013 
U. C. Dhyani, J.
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate present 
for the appellant. 
Mr. Alok Mahara, Advocate present for 
the respondents. 
Present second appeal has been preferred 
by the plaintiffs-appellants being aggrieved 
against the judgment and decree dated 
11.07.2013 passed by Additional District Judge / 
Special Judge, C.B.I., Nainital in Civil Appeal 
No. 55 / 2008, whereby the judgment and decree 
dated 04.11.2008 passed by learned Civil Judge 
(JD), Haldwani, District Nainital was affirmed. 
Admit the second appeal on the following 
substantial questions of law: 
“(i) As to whether both the courts 
below have erred in law in dismissing 
the suit on the ground of limitation 
ignoring/condoning the time spent in 
revenue courts seeking the 
declaration of being Bhumidhar with 
transferable rights incidentally 
challenging the disputed sale deed 
and ignoring the provisions of Order 
7 Rule 6 CPC read with Article 58, 59 
of the Limitation Act? 
(ii) As to whether a power of 
attorney holder entrusted with the 
management of the property can 
execute the sale deed of the property 
in absence of any specific rights of 
transfer being mentioned in the power 
of the attorney?  It is provided, as an interim measure, 
that the parties shall maintain status quo over 
the suit property till further orders of this 
Court. Stay application is disposed of. 
 Lower Court Record be summoned. List 
after the Lower Court Record is received. 
 (U. C. Dhyani, J.) 
 04.08.2015 SH
